payload.text: Requirement: Users can submit feedback text from the app. Store submissions in DynamoDB and email a weekly digest to the product team via SendGrid.  No designs. Please make reasonable assumptions for everything else and propose the spec NOW via save_spec. Keep the storage and email choices exactly as stated: DynamoDB for submissions, SendGrid for the weekly digest.

findings.issue: DynamoDB is not on the approved services list and requires architecture board sign-off before use. The spec uses DynamoDB as the sole persistence layer for feedback submissions.
findings.suggested_text: Replace DynamoDB with Amazon RDS (PostgreSQL) as the persistence layer for feedback submissions. Create a `feedback` table with columns: `feedback_id` (UUID v4, PK), `user_id` (text), `submitted_at` (timestamptz), `feedback_text` (text), `app_version` (text), `user_agent` (text). If DynamoDB is strongly preferred, obtain architecture board sign-off before proceeding and document the approval in this spec.

findings.issue: SendGrid is not an approved AWS service. Using an external third-party email provider for transactional/digest email is not covered by the approved service list and has not been assessed for data residency, credential handling, or compliance. Customer feedback data (including userId and feedbackText) would be transmitted outside the AWS eu-west-1 boundary to SendGrid's infrastructure.
findings.suggested_text: Replace SendGrid with Amazon SES (if approved after architecture board review) or raise a separate architecture decision record (ADR) to formally approve an external email provider. Note that any approved external provider must be assessed for data residency — PII (userId, feedbackText) must not leave eu-west-1 without a documented DPIA and DPA with the provider. The SendGrid API key must be stored in AWS Secrets Manager, not in environment variables or Lambda configuration.

findings.issue: No encryption-at-rest specification is provided for the DynamoDB table. Bank policy requires encryption at rest for all data stores. DynamoDB must be configured with a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) in eu-west-1.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'Data persistence' section: 'The DynamoDB table (or replacement RDS instance) must be encrypted at rest using a customer-managed KMS key (CMK) created in eu-west-1. The CMK ARN must be recorded in the infrastructure manifest. SSE-KMS must be explicitly enabled at table/instance creation; do not rely on AWS-managed default keys.'

findings.issue: Data residency is unspecified. The spec does not pin any resource to eu-west-1. DynamoDB tables, Lambda functions, API Gateway, EventBridge rules, and any SES/SendGrid integration must all be explicitly constrained to eu-west-1. Without this, customer feedback data (including userId and free-text) could be created in a non-compliant region.
findings.suggested_text: Add an 'Infrastructure constraints' section: 'All AWS resources created for this feature (API Gateway, Lambda, DynamoDB/RDS, EventBridge rule, KMS keys, CloudWatch log groups) must be deployed exclusively in eu-west-1. IaC templates must hard-code the region and CI/CD pipelines must reject deployments targeting any other region.'

findings.issue: No TLS / HTTPS requirement is stated for the POST /feedback and GET /feedback/digest endpoints. Bank policy requires TLS 1.2+ for all client-to-service and service-to-service communication. HTTP endpoints are a blocker.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'API endpoints' section: 'All endpoints must be served exclusively over HTTPS via Amazon API Gateway with a minimum TLS policy of TLS_1_2. HTTP (port 80) must be disabled or redirected. The API Gateway resource policy must deny requests that do not use TLS 1.2+.'

findings.issue: GET /feedback/digest is described as 'Internal/admin only' but no access control mechanism is specified. Without an enforced authz layer this endpoint could expose all user feedback (including userId and feedbackText) publicly.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'API endpoints' table note for GET /feedback/digest: 'This endpoint must be protected by an API Gateway resource policy restricting access to the digest Lambda's IAM execution role only (via aws:SourceArn condition). It must not be reachable from the public internet. Consider implementing it as a direct Lambda-to-RDS/DynamoDB call without an API Gateway route entirely, removing the public surface area.'

findings.issue: Amazon EventBridge is implied by the spec ('scheduled AWS EventBridge rule') but is not on the approved services list. It requires architecture board confirmation, or the scheduling mechanism must be replaced with an approved alternative.
findings.suggested_text: Add an open question or note: 'EventBridge Scheduler/Rules are not yet on the approved services list. Confirm architecture board approval before use, or document approval inline. Alternative: use a CloudWatch Events scheduled rule if that is covered under existing approvals.'

findings.issue: No audit logging strategy is described for the digest Lambda function. Bank policy requires structured logs to CloudWatch Logs for all new service integrations. The spec mentions CloudWatch alarms on retry exhaustion but does not specify structured logging for normal digest execution, SendGrid call outcomes, or item counts.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'Weekly digest' section: 'The digest Lambda must emit structured JSON logs to a CloudWatch Logs log group (e.g., /aws/lambda/feedback-digest) for every execution, including: execution timestamp, number of items queried, SendGrid request status, retry attempts, and any errors. Log retention must be set to at least 90 days. A CloudWatch dashboard should surface digest success/failure metrics.'

findings.issue: No audit logging strategy is described for the POST /feedback Lambda function. Submission events (success, validation failure, persistence error) should emit structured logs to CloudWatch Logs.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'API endpoints' section: 'The Lambda handling POST /feedback must emit structured JSON logs (submission ID, userId hash or "anonymous", HTTP status returned, error type if any) to CloudWatch Logs at /aws/lambda/feedback-submit. Do not log raw feedbackText to avoid PII in log streams unless log streams are themselves access-controlled.'

findings.issue: The SendGrid API key must be stored securely. The spec does not mention how the key is provided to the Lambda function. Storing it as a Lambda environment variable in plaintext violates bank policy (Secrets Manager required for all secrets in production).
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'Weekly digest' section: 'The SendGrid API key must be stored in AWS Secrets Manager (eu-west-1) and retrieved at Lambda invocation time via the Secrets Manager API. It must never be placed in Lambda environment variables, SSM Parameter Store standard parameters, or source control. The Lambda execution role must have secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission scoped to the specific secret ARN.'

findings.issue: The spec stores 'userId' and free-text 'feedbackText' (potentially containing PII) in DynamoDB. No data retention / TTL policy is defined. Open question 5 acknowledges this but it is unresolved. Without a TTL or retention policy the bank may be in breach of data minimisation obligations. GDPR deletion is explicitly out of scope, which is acceptable for now, but the absence of any retention boundary is a risk.
findings.suggested_text: Resolve Open Question 5 before approval: define a DynamoDB TTL attribute (e.g., `expiresAt`) set to submittedAt + retention period (recommended: 12 months or as advised by DPO). Add this field to the item schema in the 'Data persistence' section.

findings.issue: No IAM least-privilege policy is specified for the Lambda execution roles. Without explicit scoping, developers may default to broad resource ARNs (e.g., dynamodb:* on *). Bank policy flags wildcard resource ARNs as a warning.
findings.suggested_text: Add an 'IAM roles' section: 'The feedback-submit Lambda execution role must be granted only: dynamodb:PutItem on the specific feedback table ARN. The feedback-digest Lambda execution role must be granted only: dynamodb:Query/Scan on the specific feedback table ARN, and secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the specific SendGrid secret ARN. No wildcard (*) resource ARNs are permitted in any policy statement.'

findings.issue: Open question 4 (rate limiting) is unresolved. Anonymous submissions with no rate limit expose the feedback API to spam and cost amplification (DynamoDB writes, SendGrid email volume). Consider AWS WAF on API Gateway or API Gateway usage plans.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'API endpoints' section or resolve in open questions: 'API Gateway usage plans or AWS WAF rate-based rules should be applied to POST /feedback to limit submissions per IP to a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 per hour). For authenticated users, enforce per-Cognito-sub limits via a Lambda authorizer check against a counter in RDS or via API Gateway usage plans keyed on the JWT sub claim.'

findings.issue: The digest queries DynamoDB by submittedAt (a non-key attribute). Without a Global Secondary Index (GSI) on submittedAt this requires a full table scan, which is inefficient and costly at scale.
findings.suggested_text: Add to the 'Data persistence' section: 'Create a DynamoDB GSI with submittedAt as the sort key (and a static partition key such as a week-bucket string, e.g., "YYYY-Www") to support efficient time-range queries for the digest job without full table scans. Alternatively, if migrating to RDS PostgreSQL, index the submitted_at column.'
